liam: heads up — after switching kernel selector to prefer rope_fast_v2 for ROPE workloads we saw a small but consistent degradation for long sequences (>=4096). error spikes in prod qps on ded-agg: latency p99 + tail OOMs :warning:

liam: repro locally on bf16 on A10G with batch=1 seq=8192, got NaNs in attention softmax and some huge exponentials. suspect accumulation precision in the new fused kernel. logs attached below. :eyes:

liam: logs: ```
E ATTENTION: softmax_sum inf at head=2 step=1023 exp_max=1.2e+37
E KERNEL: acc overflow while accumulating dot-product sum (bf16 path)
```

sophia: thanks liam — good catch. did the older rope_ref kernel (non-fused) avoid this?

liam: yes, rope_ref runs in fp32 accumulate + bf16 multiply and is stable at seq=8192. rope_fast_v2 uses bf16 accumulation with tiled warp reductions to cut memory and latency. perf win there but numerical fragility appears.

rahul: quick triage idea: can we force the kernel selector to fallback to rope_ref when sequence_length > threshold? that buys time while we fix numerical path.

marie: agree. we already expose kernel_selector.policy in config. we can add a new policy rule: if model.posenc in {ROPE, Rotary} and seq_len > 2048 and dtype==bf16 then prefer rope_ref. low risk toggle.

chen: adding to that — also add an assert in the fused kernel to detect inf/very large exp_max and early abort to safe fallback (return status to runtime) instead of silently producing NaNs. will log metrics to ops.

liam: good. i ran microbenchmarks: rope_fast_v2 gives ~18% lower p99 on seq=1024 but degrades to wrong outputs at >=4096 in bf16. fp32 path is stable but 30% slower.

rahul: tradeoff: roll back selector for long sequences vs. fix kernel (longer). prefer fast mitigation: selector rule + add unit regression test for seq=8192 that checks for non-NaN and stable softmax sums.

marie: @ops-bot can you schedule a canary config push to ded-agg that applies the selector rule? small percentage initially.

ops-bot: acknowledged. will roll config to 5% of ded-agg nodes in 10m. monitoring alert on "attention_nan_rate" and p99 latency.

liam: created a small reproducer in runtime/tests/integration/rope_long_seq_test.cc — pushes seq=8192 with random input seed and asserts finite softmax. pushed to liam/rope-long-repro branch.

chen: tech details we should consider for a proper kernel fix:
- switch accumulation to fp32 for the reduction stage even on bf16 tile ops (cast before sum, then cast down)
- apply log-sum-exp shift: compute m = max(logit), subtract m before exponentiating (we already do this but fused kernel uses a blocked max that can miss global max if not reduced carefully)
- use pairwise summation to reduce rounding error
- add small epsilon when dividing by sum to avoid div-by-zero artifacts

liam: note: fused kernel's blocked max issue is likely due to per-tile max produced in bf16 and not being reduced in higher precision. yields wrong m leading to huge exps.

sophia: good checklist. can we get a prototype patch that does fp32 max/reduce across tiles and keeps the rest bf16? measure perf overhead. if overhead < 7% it's acceptable given stability.

chen: i'll hack on that today. also will add a runtime feature flag kernel.experimental.force_fp32_reduce to let us test perf vs stability in prod.

marie: action items:
- chen: prototype fp32 reduce + pairwise sum, push PR and perf numbers (ETA EOD)
- liam: open selector-rule config PR and unit test (done) and coordinate canary with ops-bot
- rahul: add e2e regression in CI for long-seq ROPE and ensure it gates canary rollout
- sophia: update kernel-selector RFC doc with fallback policy and the selector rule semantics

liam: one more note — customers on Dedicated with high seq workloads should see no user-facing regression; we'll backfill a targeted rollout and notify SEs.

marie: thanks team. once chen's prototype shows numbers we can decide whether to keep fp32 reduce permanently or only on long sequences. keep communicating in this thread. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary config applied to 5% of ded-agg nodes (group ded-agg-a). monitoring hooks enabled.

chen: pushed draft PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4821 — bench numbers: seq=4096 batch=1 bf16: rope_fast_v2 baseline p99 42ms -> with fp32-reduce 45ms (+7.1%) and no NaNs. adding more runs.

liam: perfect. looks like the right tradeoff. i'll update incident notes and ping SEs.

sophia: i'll follow up with a short RFC addendum describing the selector thresholds and kernel invariants.

liam: thank you all — keeping this open until we merge the fix and reach 0 attention_nan_rate in canary.

chen: will report back in ~6 hours with extended perf matrix.
